sentences.text: The genus is named Brasilotitan, combining references to Brazil and Greek Titans, while its type species, Brasilotitan nemophagus, derives its name from Greek words meaning pasture and eat to reflect its plant-eating habits.
This animal was a small sauropod, estimated to be less than 12 meters long, and possessed an L-shaped mandible that produced a squared-off snout, a feature shared with other titanosaurs.
The symphyseal region of the dentary in Brasilotitan is slightly twisted medially, a feature never previously recorded in any titanosaur.
The neural spines of the cervical vertebrae in Brasilotitan are relatively low.
Evidence of puncture marks and nearby theropod teeth suggests the holotype skeleton was scavenged by theropods before burial.
William R. Nava collected a partial sauropod skeleton in 2000 near Presidente Prudente in São Paulo state.
Elaine B. Machado and colleagues described the remains as the new species Brasilotitan nemophagus in 2013.
The holotype specimen MPM 125R is a partial skeleton including a dentary, cervical and sacral vertebrae, pelvic fragments, and an ungual phalanx.
Based on lower jaw morphology, Brasilotitan appears to be closely related to Antarctosaurus and Bonitasaura.
Phylogenetic analyses identify Brasilotitan as the sister taxon of the Brazilian titanosaur Uberabatitan.
Filippi et al. classified Brasilotitan within "Clade A", a group of titanosaurs characterized by square jaws.
Brasilotitan lived during the Late Cretaceous (early Maastrichtian) in the Adamantina Formation of Brazil.
Brasilotitan nemophagus lived approximately between 94 and 84 million years ago during the Turonian and Santonian stages in what is now South America.
The time range for Brasilotitan is estimated from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago).
In 2017, Brusatte and colleagues suggested that some sauropod fossils attributed to the Adamantina Formation may actually originate from the Presidente Prudente Formation.
